LESSON: LETTER FORMATION

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: WRITING
Topic 4.6: Letter formation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Letter formation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LETTER FORMATION
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Letter formation helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LETTER FORMATION
Study Letter formation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Letter formation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Letter formation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Letter formation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Letter formation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Letter formation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Letter formation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Letter formation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Letter formation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Demonstrate ability to singing related rhymes. incorporate letter form letters correctly in •.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
